title.narrative: WindAC Africa Conference delivers cutting edge research in the form of no less than 10 paper presentations alongside industry expert presentations. A panel of experts (Scientific Advisory Committee - SAC) will evaluate all presentations and the highest ranked paper will be presented to an industry journal for publication.
The successful implementation of 10 paper presentations.

target.value: The aim for 2023 is to have wider reach, resulting in deeper impact. We hope to see the number of attendees grow at least 100 pax and based on funding, attendance is offered free of charge.

actual.value: - 90 registered attendees - 20 abstracts received - 14 full paper submissions - 21 Speakers, comprising of both paper presentations and expert speakers - 9 presentations - 33 delegates attended SARETEC site visit - 30 delegates attended the Hopefield Wind Farm site visit.

title.narrative: SAWEA embarked on establishing an energyDRIVE Mpumalanga route which aims to reach Grades 9-12 students across 10-12 schools in the Mpumalanga Province.
Amplified reach in the region - increasing the number of learners and communities positively engaged on renewable energy and how it can positively impact their lives.

target.value: 10-12 schools; 1500-2000 learners; Mpumalanga Green Cluster Agency endorsement

actual.value: - Energy DRIVE Mpumalanga will be implemented alongside Eskom. - While we have identified 40 schools, the exact route will be determined and finalized pending consultation with the Department of Education in Mpumalanga, Mpumalanga Green Agency, and local authorities with final approval by Eskom. - Eskom are currently in the process of verifying schools within a 90km radius to Eskom plants and will look to include schools outside of this radius as well. - The dates for implementation are in discussion as the intention is to have Energy Drive Mpumalanga coincides with Eskoms Career Expos thus amplifying impact and participation.

target.value: 10-12 schools; 1500-2000 learners; Mpumalanga Green Cluster Agency endorsement

actual.value: Energy DRIVE Mpumalanga was delivered in 2 parts: Part 1 in May 2024 and Part 2 in July-August 2024. Energy Drive Mpumalanga 2024 reached 18649 learners and visited 38 schools. On 27 May 2024 - Ambassador Krone joined the Energy Drive and presented opening remarks at Kwanala Primary School.

title.narrative:
The project aims to educate, create awareness and inspire learners and graduates to take interest in renewable power, The overall goal is to create awareness of pertinent informations on the South African wind power market, and promotion of socio-economic development and transformation through wind power.
To further introduce, educate and capacitate scholars and exchange of knowledge to industry experts on renewable power and its benefits.

Positioning wind as a contributor to global decarbonization strategies, through providing education and awareness of renewable energy sources to learners in high school, internship opportunities for graduates, access to academia through research studies and Wind Academic conference, and networking and information sharing of key industry stakeholders.

target.value: - WindAc Conference in October 2023 - Mpumalanga EnergyDRIVE from July 2023 to August 2023 - 4 x Networking Events from June to July 2024 - Wind Industry Internship Programme placements from September 2023 to December 2024 - One research study conducted between August 2023 to September 2024
- Wind Academic Conference - Energy Drive Mpumalanga - SAWEA Networking Events - SAWEA Wind Industry Internship Programme - SAWEA Research Studies

title.narrative: Networking events: a new initiative aimed at creating a platform for open engagement amongst industry peers and stakeholders addressing and / or highlighting topical issues pertinent to the wind energy industry.
Each event is linked to a SAWEA Working Group to allow for an integrated industry approach to topics being discussed.

target.value: At least 4 x networking events successfully implemented.

actual.value: All four of the 4 agreed networking events have taken place. The first was a CEO Breakfast Roundtable hosted in Cape Town with high level attendance from project developers, including the CEO of SAPVIA. The discussion centred on investment challenges and opportunities within the South African renewable energy market. The second was an IRP Engagement Forum co-hosted by SAPVIA with sessions in Johannesburg and Cape Town and focused on gathering wind and solar industry experts to provide feedback and inputs ahead of the 23 March deadline submission. The Ambassador virtually presented opening remarks for the IRP session. Each networking session had about 50-70 persons in attendance. The 3rd networking session took place during South Africa's women's month with the topic: Women leading the Just Energy Transition - the event took place in Sandton, Johannesburg with a a good attendance. The event was opened by the Danish Embassies Deputy head of mission and followed by a panel discussion. The last networking event was themed - Turbine Talks Member End of Year Networking Event. The session reflected on the past years achievements and challenges, while discussion future prospects and opportunities for the wind energy sector in South Africa.

target.value: At least 4 x networking events successfully implemented.

title.narrative: Wind Industry Internship Programme (WIIP) is a 12-month learnership programme in collaboration with the EWSETA providing graduates the opportunity to link up with renewable energy companies to obtain practical work experience aligned to their field of vocation. It also includes a short 10-day skills programme introducing work readiness modules.

Applications are submitted via online forms for both learners and host companies to enable the match-matchmaking process. Quarterly reports depicting each learner's progress alongside project reports are submitted to EWSETA in tandem with EWSETA reporting templates. This makes tracking a project of this scale and magnitude structured and easy to present.

actual.value: SAWEA managed to successfully place 30 learners for the 2024 Wind Industry Internship programme, inclusive of a 10 day work readiness skills programme successfully completed with accredited training service provider. Technical training sessions to follow with content and schedule being finalised - these will roll out per quarter between March 2024 and February 2025.
